newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says U.S. messages will not go unanswered.
newsitem.headline: Iran says U.S. messages will not go unanswered.

text.p: Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said on Sunday Iran was ready to answer any messages sent by the United States through its official interest section in Tehran.
"If they (the United States) send a message to us through their interest section (at the Swiss Embassy), it will not remain unanswered," Velayati told reporters.
"In case of necessity, it will be replied through our interest section (at the Pakistani Embassy) in Washington," he said.

Velayati was responding to a question about remarks by U.S. Assistant Secretary of State Robert Pelletreau in October that he was hopeful the United States would begin dialogue with Iran within U.S. President Bill Clinton's second term.
The United States broke diplomatic ties with Iran in 1980 over the seizure of the U.S. embassy in Tehran by Moslem militants who held 52 American hostages for 444 days.
